observation.visible_scene: A tan/beige surface (wall or curved panel) fills the upper frame, crossed by a narrow vertical specular light streak. A white sheet of paper occupies the lower portion of the frame, on which a curved, V-shaped band of dispersed colored light (blue-white-yellow, rainbow-like) is visible near the paper's top edge. From mid-segment onward a thumb/finger appears at the paper's lower-left corner, holding it.
visible_changes: The white paper edge rises from below the frame (first appearing around t=0.27 s) until it settles occupying roughly the lower half of the view by t=1.5 s, then holds steady.

The rainbow-colored light pattern on the paper becomes progressively more visible as the paper enters view, then remains largely stable in shape and position relative to the paper's top edge, with only minor shifts.
The vertical light streak on the tan background drifts leftward across the frame over the segment (from center toward the left third).
A thumb appears at the lower-left edge of the paper around t=1.6 s and persists to the end, indicating the paper is being held.
The overall framing shifts slightly (paper rising, streak moving left), consistent with a small camera tilt/pan, though the source of the motion is not directly visible.
outside_clip_unknowns: The light source or object producing the rainbow dispersion pattern is not shown.
Whether the paper is physically lifted or the camera tilts to reveal it is not determinable.
Events before t=0 and after t=2.67 s are outside the excerpt.
uncertain_details: Object motion vs camera motion is ambiguous; the tan surface's identity (wall vs curved object) is unclear.
The colored band on the paper could be a reflection or a projected spectrum; the clip does not disambiguate.
Small changes in the rainbow pattern's shape may be camera angle effects rather than pattern motion.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
